title: one pane parser, not two — the duplication the detector named

AC1.note: utils/pane-parse.ts exports CHROME_PATTERNS, isChrome, parseLine, parseStatus (plus SCRIPT_WRAPPER_PATTERNS and MAX_STATUS_LINES); both monitors import from it

AC2.note: neither monitor contains any of the twelve patterns, isChrome, parseLine or parseStatus — verified by grep and by the dupes report

AC3.note: T5: dupes 19 -> 5, zero shared by the two monitors; the drop is 14, above the twelve required

AC4.note: parseLine strips on every path; tests cover an escape before the marker for spinner and tool lines, and a coloured prompt still ending the parseStatus scan

AC5.note: extraChrome is a parameter; /^\x1b/ is gone and a test asserts CHROME_PATTERNS carries no escape-anchored pattern and that a stripped line still parses

AC6.note: a test asserts no earlier branch can match a line starting Error:, so the two copies' opposite orderings agreed

AC7.note: every parseLine branch covered: spinner, all tool shapes, self-tool suppression, truncation, sub-operations, agent tree, +N more, Running N agents, Tip, fall-through, tabs

AC8.note: parseStatus tested for bottom-up order, the 12-line cap, keeping the newest when capping, the prompt boundary, an ANSI-decorated prompt, and null on nothing

AC9.note: T6: three panes captured from live helyx/keryx/goodai sessions, parsed before and after — byte-identical, re-run after each of the three review fixes

AC10.note: bun run typecheck clean; bun run lint 0 errors (208 warnings, pre-existing); 696 unit tests pass, none skipped or removed
